Traverse a list to collect stations once

Unit 1 · Week 6 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Before class verify the nominated editor uses a school-approved Python/Pygame installation. Extract the whole pygame-teaching-pack.zip into a writable disposable folder. Open https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-3 and workbook.md, faded_practice.py, practice-tests.csv and readiness.csv. Run python lab_runner.py 3. Use supplied named state/runner infrastructure; no student-authored classes, paid media or assessed project code. Record device, interpreter and support. Paper traces support reasoning; live window/keyboard evidence remains necessary. The suggested 55-minute allocation is untrialled; use the supplied 50-minute adaptation when required.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Open the matching Pygame lab · Practice workbook · Test record · Readiness record

1. Collect each station once

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Run python lab_runner.py 3. Two stationary stations are at x80 and520 on y180, each24×24. The moving player is24×24; score is one per station once. This is a short bridge lab, not the assessed game or a new weighted task. Success: trace list indices, inactive flags, overlap and score, then transfer to three changed stations. 2. Retrieve traversal and accumulation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and paired explanation

Indices0,1; initialise score once in the fresh state before collecting, not inside the traversal or draw function. An empty traversal performs zero additions. Keep this short retrieval from list totals, then connect each index to a station and its active flag. Treat list position and station x as different values. 3. An active flag prevents a second score

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and predicted trace

This focused excerpt uses the supplied rules.overlaps strict predicate and list flags; overlaps matches the edge convention of pygame.Rect.colliderect. The full update constructs player=(int(state["x"]),180,24,24), checks timeout first and does this loop only in playing mode. enumerate supplies indices0,1 and positions80,520. On contact set the corresponding flag False before incrementing. Do not delete elements during traversal or add score in drawing code. 4. Trace flags and score together

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Faded worked table and paired trace

Start [True,True], score0. Touch station0: [False,True],1. Repeat same contact: unchanged. Touch station1: [False,False],2; full worked update changes mode to finished. Model first contact; pairs predict repeat and second station before running. The display may outline an inactive station, but that drawing must not alter scoring. A flag belongs to the same index as its station. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-3; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

5. Touching edges is not overlap

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict–run comparison and counterexample

At x56 the right edge is80, so edge-touch is False. At x57 the right edge is81 and there is a one-pixel overlap, so True. Use pygame.Rect(56,180,24,24).colliderect(pygame.Rect(80,180,24,24)) and then57. Strict overlap also requires vertical intersection; an x-only comparison is insufficient. This simple frame-end test can miss a fast crossing during a very large step; do not promise continuous collision physics. 6. Change to three two-point stations

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent changed task with optional support

Use the changed scaffold: active=[True,True,True], duration15000 ms, speed160, initial x40. Complete strict overlaps and the collection portion of update; retain the movement-only guard from last lab. Do not import lab_rules as a solution. Keep stationary flags in a one-dimensional list. First test rule functions without graphics; then copy the runner and adapt its rules import, station positions/list length, score denominator and labels. That runner adaptation is supplied/teacher-guided infrastructure, not a demand to build a complete game. Each station once yields2,4,6; repeated contact gives no increment. Do not remove elements while traversing. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-3; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

7. Which guard prevents repeated scoring?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question

B. A would add once per overlapping update. Require both active and overlap, then immediately make the flag False. Ask for the trace after ten repeated contacts, not just the letter. If learners confuse inactive with invisible, show that drawing and rule state are separate responsibilities. 8. Show once-only collection

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit check and explanation

Record a fresh case after feedback. In the changed lab touching x96 against station120 is False, x97 is True. Repeated contact with station0 keeps score2; all three gives6 and finished. Create two states, mutate one flag, show the other is unaffected. Record expected/actual and support in y11-3 readiness. If only a paper trace was possible, label live collision/keyboard evidence pending.
